name: Ginger
short: Pregnancy trials found no significant rise in miscarriage (with wide uncertainty), heartburn or drowsiness. A warfarin review flags possible added bleeding risk.
text: In a meta-analysis of 12 randomised trials in 1278 pregnant women with nausea, ginger did not significantly increase the risk of spontaneous abortion, heartburn or drowsiness compared with placebo. A systematic review of warfarin interactions listed ginger among foods and herbs for which healthcare professionals should be aware of an increased bleeding risk, while a separate review of supplements and bleeding judged the evidence on ginger's overall bleeding risk to be conflicting. The warfarin review advised patients to seek advice from their healthcare professionals when starting any new herb or supplement.
